correctness.rationale: The Alexander dual of the ordinary 3-cut complex is exactly the complex K_p of subsets whose every triple induces a connected C_{4p}^p graph. Independently reconstructed K_2 with f-cardinalities (8,28,32,10), verified all 20 specified elementary free-face removals, and checked the residual connected closed triangulated surface has f=(8,18,12), circular vertex links and Euler characteristic 2, hence K_2≃S². Rotation by one fixes no nonempty face, giving its degree -1 by Lefschetz. The alternating singleton/(p-1)-vertex 8-block quotients and sections are weak graph homomorphisms; source-edge and section checks were independently verified for 2<=p<=35, while the symbolic distance threshold >p for jumps across 3 blocks proves every p>=2. Relative offsets t=s, t=s-1 and all others respectively give identity, odd rotation and parity-simplex maps, hence deg(Q_s E_t)=δ_{st}-δ_{t,s-1}. Independently computed 338349 complete signed simplicial Lefschetz degrees for all s,t and 2<=p<=100 (including 5049 of each ±1), matching the formula. The principal (p-1)x(p-1) minor is unit triangular, giving a split Z^{p-1} in H_2(K_p;Z), and combinatorial Alexander duality+UCT give a split Z^{p-1} in reduced H_{4p-5}(Δ_3(C_{4p}^p);Z). Since Δ is pure of dimension 4p-4, this nonzero lower homology obstructs shellability. Finite calculations corroborate but do not replace the symbolic all-p proof; p=2 boundary included.

value.rationale: A recent explicit conjecture predicted that the critical n=4p three-cut complexes should be non-shellable and have wedge topology. This theorem settles the non-shellability implication uniformly for the natural infinite family p>=2, with an integral primitive direct-summand mechanism rather than merely finite ranks. The exact splitting is a reusable structural obstruction; it is not just a table recomputation or arbitrary slice. It does not claim the stronger conjectured homotopy type or entire Betti group.

limitations: No complete homotopy classification, exact Betti rank, torsion determination or extension to n!=4p.
Finite checks do not prove all-p behavior; all-p proof is algebraic/geometric and independently reconstructed.
